title: Anti-asthma drug montelukast induces autistic behaviors via disrupting neuronal retinoic acid signaling.
authors: Hao, Zi-Jian; Wu, Qiong-Hui; Li, Ya-Li; Guo, Zhen-Ming; Li, Zheng-Wei; Wang, Gui; Meng, Meng; Yuan, Shi-Lin; Wufuer, Yilimire; Zhang, Meng-Huan; Chen, Jie; Yang, Ting; Chen, Meng-Xia; Zhu, Jiang; Qi-Hang, Wang; Li, Qiu; Yu, Shi-Hu; Lu, Min; Xiong, Hai-Yi; Feng, Yu-Ru; Dong, Meng-Qi; Xu, Jun-Hao; Xu, Jia-Lin; Chen, Li; Yang, Han-Ting; Miao, Jing-Kun; Zhu, Hong; Yang, Bo; Zhao, Hui-Ying; Shi, Xiao-Ming; Bian, Shan; Li, Ting-Yu; Hu, Rong-Gui
one_liner_zh: 该文研究抗哮喘药孟鲁司特通过干扰维甲酸信号诱导自闭症行为，虽含分子对接验证药物与RARA受体互作，但核心是药物-受体而非蛋白质-DNA互作体系，且无AI或物理模拟方法，仅边缘相关。
abstract: Autism spectrum disorders (ASD) affect approximately 1.0% of children worldwide with still increasing global prevalence. The fact that genetic factors contribute to less than 50% of ASD suggests some critical yet enigmatic roles of non-genetic factors in ASD etiology. Here, we reported that montelukast (MTK), a cysteinyl leukotriene receptor antagonist and one of the most commonly prescribed anti-asthma drugs, potently disrupted neuronal retinoic acid (RA) signaling and altered synaptic plasticity of the primary neurons from rat pre-frontal cortex (PFC). Prenatal or early postnatal exposure to MTK induced autistic-like behaviors in wild-type rats, which could be significantly alleviated by supplementing all-trans retinoic acid (atRA). MTK altered neuronal RA signaling and forebrain patterning in brain organoids derived from human embryonic stem cells through antagonizing RA in RA signaling. Meanwhile, molecular docking followed by biochemical validation strongly indicated that MTK could physically interact with RA receptors (RARs), e.g. RA receptor alpha (RARA). Furthermore, multi-center survey with a large Chinese ASD cohort suggested that MTK administration during early childhood might indeed increase the risk of ASD in children. Altogether, our findings have not only established MTK use as a yet unrecognized risk factor for human ASD, but highlighted the key importance of safer use of medicines to prevent ASD.
abstract_zh: 自闭症谱系障碍（ASD）影响全球约1.0%的儿童，且全球患病率仍在持续上升。遗传因素对ASD的贡献不足50%，这一事实提示非遗传因素在ASD病因学中扮演着某些关键但尚不明确的角色。在此，我们报道了孟鲁司特（MTK），一种半胱氨酰白三烯受体拮抗剂且为最常用的抗哮喘药物之一，能够有效干扰神经元视黄酸（RA）信号传导，并改变大鼠前额叶皮层（PFC）原代神经元的突触可塑性。产前或出生后早期暴露于MTK可诱导野生型大鼠出现自闭症样行为，而补充全反式视黄酸（atRA）可显著缓解这些行为。MTK通过拮抗RA信号传导中的RA，改变了人胚胎干细胞来源的脑类器官中的神经元RA信号传导和前脑模式形成。同时，分子对接及随后的生化验证强烈表明，MTK可与RA受体（RARs）发生物理相互作用，例如RA受体α（RARA）。此外，针对大型中国ASD队列的多中心调查提示，儿童早期使用MTK确实可能增加儿童患ASD的风险。综上所述，我们的发现不仅确立了MTK使用作为人类ASD的一个尚未被认识的风险因素，而且强调了安全用药以预防ASD的关键重要性。
